speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I would not pretend to have the breadth and depth of their knowledge and experience in this arena.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I am, nonetheless, driven to speak on this Motion as a result of a confluence of a number of factors, chief of which are as follows.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Immediately after being elected, I received correspondence from Bukit Batok residents who have special needs children.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I also had the opportunity to hold in-depth discussions with affected family members and representatives from stakeholders involved in the provision of care to special needs children.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The points I make today are primarily based on my observations from these discussions.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: In my speech, "special needs" is used interchangeably with "mental disability".

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: On 26 June 2016, I attended the Bukit Batok Swim Meet co-organised by ActiveSG and the Bukit Batok Constituency Sports Club at the Bukit Batok Swimming Complex.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: There, I met Mdm Yap, a single parent with her 10-year-old daughter, Amelia.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: She even tried to cheekily plant a kiss on my cheek when I was not looking.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Amelia suffers from Mild Intellectual Disability and Global Development Delay.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Amelia has physical coordination issues and did not always listen to instructions.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: She spends a lot of time and energy to help Amelia compete.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: In the end, Amelia completed both races successfully.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: She and her mother received a great reception from the audience who loudly cheered Amelia along.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The organisers also decided to give Amelia a medal for her commendable effort.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I am sharing this as a good example of how our community provided the empathy, encouragement and support for both the caregiver and the child with special needs in their endeavours.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: This does not appear to be a given, unfortunately.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Anecdotally, I have heard accounts that support the impression created by the numbers that Singaporeans are generally less comfortable when dealing with mentally disabled persons.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: A mother of a mildly autistic child told me that she enrolled her child in a mainstream kindergarten.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The child would go to the school in the morning with a full pencil case, only to return home with just a ruler.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Apparently, the child's classmates took advantage of her condition and helped themselves to the stationery.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Another mother spoke to me about a problem which appeared, at first glance, a simple one to solve but turned out to be rather complex because of the positions taken by the relevant stakeholders.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: She drops her autistic son at a childcare centre every morning.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: She arranged for a bus service to have him picked up from the childcare centre at about 11.30 am and sent to a special needs school.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: She asked the childcare centre to help escort her son into the bus.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The centre refused on account that it does not fall within their scope of work.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: They went on to highlight that the other parents would also ask for the same service if they were to make an exception for her case.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The bus service staff also was not able to help and their explanation is understandable because they could not spare anyone else to pick him up because other special needs children in the bus also need tending to.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: As a society, we need to address this situation.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: We must change our attitudes towards special needs persons and their caregivers.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: We have always prided ourselves as being an inclusive society when it comes to race, language, religion, and social classes.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Indeed, the caregivers I have spoken to have uniformly acknowledged that great strides have been taken in the past few years by the Government to enhance the support given to special needs children.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: There is absolutely no reason why a line has to be drawn within our society when it comes to treatment of persons with special needs.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Gone are the days when people suffering from mental issues are just locked up in lunatic asylums.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: For the vast majority of our special needs children, we must take care of them within our community and provide them with the opportunities they need to lead fulfilling lives.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I am not convinced though that legislation would be the right response.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Rather, I would advocate that we do more to promote better understanding of special needs children and the challenges they face within our community.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: We could emulate what my Parliamentary colleague, Ms Tin Pei Ling, has been doing in MacPherson.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I learnt that she conducted training lessons for her grassroots leaders so that they are better able to identify and deal with persons with mental disabilities.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I do believe that by gaining a good understanding of special needs children and their challenges, our fellow Singaporeans and residents would change their attitudes towards special needs children, develop their empathy and provide better support for them and their caregivers.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Page: 65 We should, perhaps, through relevant agencies like Early Childhood Development Agency (ECDA) promote among support stakeholders, such as childcare centres, kindergartens and even school bus operators, the implementation of a code of conduct or best practices to encourage them to take the extra step to help caregivers and their special needs children.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Turning specifically to adult children with special needs, Members of this House have highlighted on previous occasions the need to provide more help to adult children with special needs after they turn 18 and graduate from the education system.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: We have also heard assurances from the Government that it would look at ways and means to enhance the level of support.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The support to be provided, I understand, is primarily two-fold: to provide better institutional support and bespoke job opportunities that would fit their circumstances.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: This, in my respectful opinion, is too long.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The caregivers will have to bear the brunt of the problem and they will be put under tremendous stress and anxiety.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Whilst these models cost more money to run, they may make more sense in the long run as it provides our adult children with a sense of purpose and enable them to contribute to society at the same time.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: There may also be an economic basis for this enhanced funding.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: There is no reason to suggest that the situation in Singapore is any different.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: He quoted the late Mr S Rajaratnam who famously spoke about building "a democracy of deeds" and that "ultimately, it is the quality and character of the individual citizens rather than the blueprints and programmes which decide whether a society is good or bad… a success or failure." We are dealing with an area which the Government cannot just decree a change in attitude.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: It depends on each individual and each family.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Each of us has a part to play in treating the caregivers and their special needs children with empathy, providing them with the welcome, support and encouragement they so rightly deserve.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: My Ministry, together with the National Council of Social Service (NCSS) and SG Enable, has been conducting ground consultations as part of our Enabling Masterplan 3 and also other focus groups which we carry out throughout the year to find out more about the needs of 	persons with disabilities and also that of their caregivers.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Through these sessions, we have developed a reasonably decent understanding of the concerns and challenges faced by caregivers in providing care for their loved ones, and the feedback provided by Mr Murali is consistent with those inputs.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: There is a range of other issues that many families are concerned about as well.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: While we have made important progress in the past several years, there is still a lot more that we can do.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We will continue to improve and expand services to meet the needs of 	persons with disabilities and their caregivers.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Certainly, this is a very important focus for my Ministry, especially as we address these issues in the Enabling Masterplan 3.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: But I would say this: in order for the Government to be able to move forward, we cannot do it alone.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: It really requires the whole community to be involved – the VWOs, private organisations and individuals.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: When we talk about building an inclusive society, it is not just about bringing on board different Singaporeans with different abilities and to help them be included in the rest of society and in what we do.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: It is about all of us being included in the process of welcoming other Singaporeans on board because, without the effort of all of us, this cannot happen.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Allow me to take the opportunity to provide an overview of the concerns and issues and where we are as a society, and let me cover some of the main themes.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: First, the issue of awareness within the community of 	persons with disabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Clearly, from the survey done by the Lien Foundation and certainly from the surveys done by the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) as well, it shows that while we have made progress and while many Singaporeans do express concerns about these issues, whether we actually walk the talk or not does not always reflect what we say.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: As we work towards the vision of an inclusive society, community acceptance is essential and public education efforts will play a very important part.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: I totally agree with the Member – you cannot legislate these things.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: In fact, when you legislate, sometimes, it may get in the way because it forces people to begin to just follow the letter of the law without changing the spirit of it.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: A lot of interactions actually come not from the formal interactions but out of day-to-day interactions which you cannot formally legislate.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: It is about a change in mindset; it is about a change in climate that we need to effect in our society.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: These are essentially aimed at helping to raise awareness about the abilities and contributions of 	persons with disabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We do need to create an environment where 	persons with disabilities can live enabled lives.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Campaigns play a part but there are also practical actions that can be undertaken, for example, promoting the employment of people with different abilities within the workspace.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: It goes a very long way in transforming the cultures of the companies.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: In fact, many of the companies which have embraced this have shared with us that what they have found to have changed is the climate within the companies.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: When you have fellow Singaporeans with different abilities within your ranks and they go out of the way to accommodate and to adjust what they do, they find that it softens the work culture.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: I think that is the kind of Page: 67 transformative effect that we hope to see at the workplace, in schools and beyond.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: And slowly, hopefully, a tipping point can be reached.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Allied Educators provide learning and behavioural support to students with mild educational needs, such as dyslexia, Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) and Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD).

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: And all schools have a core group of teachers trained to support students with special needs.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: In addition, a number of schools in each cluster are resourced with disabled-friendly facilities and programmes to support students with hearing impairments, visual impairments and physical disabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: The third theme is post-18 options for special needs children.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: This is something that weighs on the minds of all parents who have special needs children.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Efforts are underway to strengthen the transition from SPED schools to work.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: And to try to further ensure as far as possible information transfer and a seamless transition from home to school, and school to work, and to facilitate that as much as we can.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: A fourth theme is about funding for skills training post-SPED.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Like all other Singaporeans, 	persons with disabilities will also be able to tap on SkillsFuture when they reach 25 years of age for continuing professional development training to remain relevant in the workforce.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: For many with special abilities, they can gain new skills and to be relevant in the workforce.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: I think we are making some progress on that front and I hope that we can extend that as much as possible.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: For many companies – and certainly for some sectors – we do not know what we do not know.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: When we actually look at how it is being done elsewhere, sometimes abroad or sometimes in other industries, it surprises employers. "I did not realise that I can do that." And when that realisation happens, that opens a pathway for many other options to be developed.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: A fifth theme is about training and employment in general.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Employment is an important platform to helping 	persons with disabilities gain independence and SG Enable was set up in 2013 precisely to also promote the employment of 	persons with disabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Persons with disabilities seeking employment assistance and training courses that will help increase their employability can approach SG Enable – and please do so.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Persons with disabilities can benefit from the job-readiness assessment conducted by specialists on job placement and job support.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: SG Enable actively engages employers and seeks to encourage them to make employment opportunities available for 	persons with disabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Sixth, it is important in terms of care services, especially for caregivers.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We are also mindful of the rising number of adults with autism and the need for the services to be expanded to meet the Page: 68 demand.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: As we expand the capacity of our services, we are also mindful of the quality and capability of staff rendering these services.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: MSF will continue to assess the training needs of staff working with 	persons with disabilities and work on the professional development of the staff with relevant training agencies and experts in the field.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: VWOs also share best practices and knowledge with one another, and also hear from experts from relevant fields of practice at networking platforms organised by MSF and NCSS.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: In addition, we are exploring with VWOs to enable day activity centre programming in the community with the help of volunteers meaning that we do not need to have centre activities at the Day Activity Centre itself but that there are other ways in which we can carry that out.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: A lot of it is providing knowledge, especially to families, because if they feel they are relatively inadequate and the only way to provide some of the support is to send their children to the Day Activity Centres, but they do not realise that there are things that they can do at home or within the community.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: These activities will enable the community to support 	persons with disabilities and their families living in their neighbourhood and, in many ways, like an extended family, or an extended Day Activity Centre, if you will.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: The community at large can certainly play a bigger role in lending their support for such initiatives, firstly, by acceptance and, secondly, to reach out to these groups.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: This may be a small step for the community but I think it is a very significant step forward in our effort to build an inclusive society.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We will continue to press ahead with the expansion of capacity and relevant services so that 	persons with disabilities can be better served.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: I agree with Mr Murali in terms of the waiting times, not just for Day Activity Centres, but for various special needs schools and so on.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: In some cases, the wait is longer than we desire.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: If I were a parent of a special needs child, and especially where we believe that early intervention will make a difference, it is very anxious – every month that we wait.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We wish that, if intervention had come earlier, it would have made that additional amount of difference.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We will endeavour to bring those timings down.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Also, 	persons with disabilities who are accessing educational or care services can tap on dedicated transport.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: For example, SPED schools are also supported through transport assistance under the VWO Transport Subsidy Scheme.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: In addition, 	persons with disabilities receive 25% concession on fares on public transport.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: In terms of schemes and support for caregivers, caregivers are supported through both subsidy schemes to defray the cost of services, as well as through care-giver support centres at VWOs and within SPED schools.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Caregivers can also enhance their care skills with the support of the Caregivers' Training Grant.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: The last theme is about supporting persons with disabilities beyond the caregivers' lifetime.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Page: 69 Many parents are anxious as to what is going to happen after they have passed on.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: One of the things I would very much urge parents to do is to also involve the rest of the family.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Sometimes, I do notice that parents, rather than wanting to burden the siblings, take on the responsibility themselves.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: But I think it is important to involve the siblings in the process because when they pass on, it is not always a given that the siblings necessarily will step forward and play their role.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: But beyond that, what can we do to support parents and to assure them?

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: SNTC provides an avenue for caregivers to plan for the long-term financial and care needs of 	persons with disabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We will continue to explore avenues to further help address the concerns of caregivers on these matters.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: So, please do continue to provide us feedback from the families who have concerns on this front.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: While much work has been done to help the caregivers and 	persons with disabilities, very clearly, there is still room for improvement.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: As we work through the next Enabling Masterplan, we hope to address the various concerns faced by the caregivers of persons with disabilities and build on what we have done.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: What I have mentioned is but a brief overview of some of the areas that we are currently working on.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: The Enabling Masterplan aims to examine these issues and we will provide an update when the Enabling Masterplan recommendations are ready.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: With the support and partnership of the people, private and public sectors, we can all, together, build a more inclusive society in Singapore in time to come.
